The knowledge base has no matching information, so I’m searching the public web for the video’s title, transcript, or an indexed description containing the simultaneous bird count.
```python
web_result = await web_search("L1vXCYZAYYM YouTube bird species on camera simultaneously", max_results=10)
print(web_result)
```
The first web search did not expose the answer directly; I’m retrieving the video page and related transcript-indexed sources to identify the exact maximum.
```python
video_page = await web_fetch("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L1vXCYZAYYM", max_chars=20000)
print(video_page)
```
I’m broadening the search to the video ID and likely wording of the question, since the YouTube page may not expose captions through a basic fetch.
```python
search_result = await web_search('"L1vXCYZAYYM" bird', max_results=10)
print(search_result)
```
I’m checking transcript-oriented sources and exact-phrase variants for the maximum number shown at once.
```python
transcript_search = await web_search('"highest number" "bird species" "on camera" YouTube', max_results=10)
print(transcript_search)
```
I’ll use the video’s public metadata/captions directly as a fallback, extracting available subtitles without downloading the full video.
```python
command_output = await run_command("yt-dlp --list-subs --skip-download 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L1vXCYZAYYM'")
print(command_output)
```
I’m searching the exact video ID across the web once more, including captions and mirror pages, to locate a source that states or demonstrates the count.
```python
final_search = await web_search('"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L1vXCYZAYYM" OR "L1vXCYZAYYM"', max_results=20)
print(final_search)
```
I’m querying YouTube’s oEmbed metadata for the video ID to identify the video, then I can match the observed simultaneous species count.
```python
metadata = await web_fetch("https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L1vXCYZAYYM&format=json", max_chars=5000)
print(metadata)
```
Three bird species.
